description: Canonical mapping from canonical operation_id (artifacts/registry/operation-registry.json) to the error codes the operation MAY emit. Derived from prose error policy in zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.3 and from error-code-registry.json scope/description. Receivers of an operation SHOULD treat any error code listed here as a known reply shape; codes that map only to the universal failure surface (e.g. internal_error, service_unavailable) are not repeated per operation. cross-link target for zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.3. snapshot_capacity_exceeded applies to every event_log admission branch in the operation registry, including peer authority_forward; committed_replication and other non-admission branches do not produce it.

rules.universal_codes: Every protected operation MAY additionally return any of: unauthenticated, auth_expired, soft_logged_out, account_locked, account_suspended, account_deactivated, account_erased, did_proof_required, signature_invalid, capability_denied, schema_violation, json_invalid, query_invalid, param_missing, param_invalid, rate_limited, too_large, conflict, internal_error, service_unavailable, temporarily_unavailable, not_implemented, unsupported_feature, unsupported_event_kind, unsupported_protocol_version, operation_selector_required, unsupported_operation_version. These are the universal failure surface and are NOT repeated in each operation entry. unsupported_protocol_version applies only when the binding implements Arkret-Protocol-Version header or equivalent media-type negotiation; ServiceDescribe consumers also use the same stable code locally before capability intersection. operation_selector_required and unsupported_operation_version are binding-level pre-dispatch failures evaluated before body parsing for every canonical operation.
rules.operation_specific: operation_specific[] lists the error codes that are semantically tied to this operation's domain logic (event ingest, key claim, blob upload, push gateway, directory ingest, ...). An entry may name either a top-level code from error-code-registry.json `codes` or a sub-code from its `reason_codes` section (carried under a top-level code such as failed_precondition or schema_violation). Consumers discriminate by first matching the entry against the registry's top-level `codes` set; an entry not found there is a reason_code and matches the error reply's `reason_code` field rather than its top-level `code`. Receivers SHOULD recognize and surface these codes specifically.
rules.endpoint_aliases: Each operation entry lists its canonical HTTP method+path alias for human navigation; alternative bindings (gRPC, MQ) inherit the same error code set.
rules.operation_coverage: Every operation_id in artifacts/registry/operation-registry.json MUST appear exactly once in operations[]. An empty operation_specific[] means the operation has no domain-specific reply shape beyond the universal failure surface.

Transaction push is a service-to-service operation in both directions. Receivers MUST fail closed when the per-delivery RFC 9421 source signature is missing/invalid/outside the replay window, when the idempotency identity is replayed with a different body or receiver-derived delivery_authentication_record_digest, when the source Applet service has no active effective install, or when an Event actor falls outside the registered Applet namespace. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §7.3.1.

A changed replay for the same authenticated source Station and registration_id conflicts without mutation; invalid provider route material is rejected before durable installation. Signature and authorization failures remain on the universal failure surface.

These codes reach the caller in two places that MUST agree: as a top-level failure envelope, and as the per-device reason_code inside push_notify_outcome.outcomes[]. rate_limited also appears in that enum but stays out of this list because it is universal (see rules.universal_codes). schema_violation is likewise universal at the request/response validation layer, but intentionally is not a per-device outcome reason: malformed input or a non-conserving response invalidates the whole exchange rather than one device route.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Authenticates a fresh account handoff for the current identity-creation lease holder and performs abandonment in one transaction, without a preceding challenge operation. proof_invalid covers handoff/DPoP holder mismatch; failed_precondition covers a stale or non-holder lease/fence and a request that pins a different principal_id or did_version_id; duplicate_conflict covers reuse of request_id with a different canonical request, while an exact replay returns the recorded outcome; identity_creation_already_accepted is the stable terminal when the PCR was accepted before the abandonment transaction commits and never abandons anything.

Unknown device_pairing_request_id, a pairing_code mismatch, an expired record and a record that is no longer staged MUST all return the same not_found, so this authenticated surface stays as unenumerable as the anonymous resolve. A schema-valid target proof that fails Ed25519 decoding, signature verification, transcript reconstruction, or whose signed account_id is not byte-equal to the AccountId the presented account handoff is bound to, returns failed_precondition with reason_code proof_invalid. Missing required members remain schema_violation. The same request id replayed with different canonical content returns duplicate_conflict and MUST NOT re-attach a proof. After an id locates a retained record, code/account/transcript/signature/proof/state failures count against its private ten-failure budget without changing any of those public errors; an unknown id and a byte-identical successful retry do not count, and the tenth failure atomically expires a pending record.

Resolves an already-published DID and issues a durable single-use control challenge. proof_invalid covers handoff/DPoP holder mismatch; failed_precondition covers rate limiting and DID state that cannot be resolved at the required freshness tier; duplicate_conflict covers the same request_id with different canonical intent; did_not_found and unsupported_did_method cover resolution outcomes that MUST fail closed rather than fall back to caller-supplied history.

Reserves the DID inception operation and issues a durable single-use challenge. proof_invalid covers handoff/DPoP holder mismatch; failed_precondition covers stale or non-holder lease/fence and an operation that does not derive the claimed principal; duplicate_conflict covers request_id reuse or an attempt to replace an existing reserved operation with different bytes. Exact replay of an expired-unconsumed or consumed challenge returns identity_creation_challenge_expired or identity_creation_challenge_already_consumed respectively; replacement remains failed_precondition. Independent issuance quota exhaustion returns the common rate_limited error with the actual blocking window and zero partial writes.

Consumes the Bound AccountHandoff only after the transaction, terminal receipt and coordinator attestation match the current accepted replacement-device projection, then obtains a fresh exact-intent origin-PS revocation-gate allow before creating one DPoP-bound Standard grant. device_revocation_pending and device_revoked create no grant or issuer-ledger outcome. No temporary recovery grant exists.

Account Authority issuer-ledger session grant issuance. `principal_unknown` is returned when the required principal_id has no verified account binding; the authority must not derive or mint a DID as a fallback. Exact replay returns the byte-identical recorded live outcome after current holder/DPoP/target/digest revalidation; conflicting canonical intent is duplicate_conflict. A recorded expired outcome returns session_grant_replay_expired; revoked/superseded returns session_grant_replay_terminal; an evicted replay record returns session_grant_replay_indeterminate. None may issue a replacement under the same request identity. Proof-kind-specific validation failures remain proof_invalid or the registered Agent lifecycle/authority codes.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): the only client-visible logout entry. It validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain, and completes or durably schedules Principal-side local account/device session cleanup plus to-device/push removal. Does not create an AccountStatusRecord, emit ak.device.revoke, or erase durable device authorization. Idempotent — no domain-specific failure beyond the universal surface.

Agent runtime key pairing. Admission verifies current controller/Agent authority, the pairing handle, requested-scope disclosure, proof-of-possession and accepted authority-committed current results; backup availability is neither an input nor a gate. Pairing into an already-deactivated agent principal is terminal. Runtime replacement uses one controller-signed ak.agent.key.authorize with an exact supersedes[] set to atomically replace every prior active authorization dot and record reason=superseded_by_repairing; the service does not synthesize ak.agent.key.revoke Events.

A schema-valid target possession proof that fails Ed25519 material decoding, signature verification or reconstructed stage binding returns failed_precondition with reason_code proof_invalid. Missing required request members or signature_material shape violations remain schema_violation. Before the durable fence is installed, a retained request located by device_pairing_request_id counts code, approving-account/device, transcript, proof/stage or usable-state failures toward its private ten-failure budget. Once prepared, retryable/network failure or a missing/mismatched RealmCommit maps to temporarily_unavailable and preserves the fence; an authenticated terminal peer rejection proven zero-write removes only prepared and maps uniformly to failed_precondition with reason_code failed_precondition, while its peer reason remains private audit material rather than implementation-defined public translation. Same fence identity with another digest or holder is duplicate_conflict with zero writes. Exact completed replay returns the stored outcome, never counts and never submits a second Event.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger rotation keyed by predecessor_grant_id plus refresh_request_digest. Exact replay returns the recorded successor after current proof revalidation; a conflicting request is duplicate_conflict. One transaction creates the successor and supersedes the predecessor. A recorded successor that is expired or terminal returns the corresponding session_grant_replay_* code and never causes a second successor. The audience remains locked; logged-out or invalid holder/fresh-proof paths retain their existing errors.

Account registration validates the frozen DID operation, root control transcript, exact PCR genesis unit and InitialSessionGrantRequest; relays the unit to the Station; verifies the pcr_genesis_unit receipt; commits the one-account/one-principal binding; then obtains a fresh exact-intent origin-PS revocation-gate allow before issuing the first Standard grant from the durable issuer ledger. device_revocation_pending and device_revoked create no grant or issuer-ledger outcome.

Self-initiated account erasure entry (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). reauthentication_required rejects a session that does not satisfy the deployment's fresh high-risk action authentication policy. failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending rejects a distinct request_id while a live intent whose erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord is unsigned already exists. duplicate_conflict rejects the same request_id replayed with different canonical bytes; exact replay returns the recorded acceptance outcome. Once the record is signed, session grants are already revoked and later calls fail at authentication with account_erased from the universal surface.

Session grant/access-token revocation. Empty body revokes the current request's session grant; cross grant/device/all_sessions selectors require fresh proof and never revoke device authorization or create an AccountStatusRecord. The issuer durably records the exact mutation outcome; exact request replay returns that outcome, while the same request identity with different canonical intent returns duplicate_conflict. If replay retention no longer proves whether the mutation committed, session_grant_replay_indeterminate fails closed with zero new state changes.

OIDC code exchange for a DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant. proof_invalid covers issuer/discovery/state/nonce/redirect_uri/PKCE/body-holder/DPoP binding failures; duplicate_conflict covers reuse of request_id with different canonical request bytes. A live lease owned by another holder is a typed identity_creation_busy outcome, not an error reply.

No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. An unknown code, a wrong code, an expired record, a record belonging to another AccountId, a record that is not yet finalized and an already consumed record MUST all return the same not_found; an error shape MUST NOT reveal whether a code exists, which account it belongs to or which device it describes. Exceeding the per-caller-device, per-AccountId or per-service rate budget returns rate_limited. A code that locates no exact retained request creates no per-request counter row; after an exact lookup succeeds, account/gate/proof/staged-material/state failures count privately, and the tenth atomically expires and consumes the pending request while the reply remains the same not_found.

No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. The live DPoP-bound handoff selects the account and holder; the response is a read-only projection of durable lease or binding state.

A same-binding retry is idempotent and retains the approval_request_id and notification id. A different stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest on the same open pairing_request_id returns HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict and MUST NOT replace the pending request.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. Each call mints a fresh account-less pending record; stage, resolve and status MUST be rate limited.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. Unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record MUST all return an indistinguishable not_found.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. A record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found).
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. An unknown or non-public principal returns not_found; the response itself is evidence and never an authorization decision.

The PSI identifier query requires a per-request RFC 9421 provider-source signature despite being classified as read: unsigned, invalid and stale-window requests fail before PSI evaluation so an unauthenticated caller cannot probe the anti-enumeration surface. provider_directory remains outside this profile.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
Authority-commit operation. Current authorization and stream-head checks are evaluated atomically by the current governance Station.
Local consumers reject a DID method history that conflicts with their durable accepted prefix using service_route_fork.

These sub-reasons are returned only to a caller that already addressed an existing provisioning record with a verifiable Station acceptance attestation; third_party_invite_provisioning_already_bound is carried by duplicate_conflict and the rest by failed_precondition. An unknown or foreign provisioning_id stays the uniform non-enumerable not_found of third-party-invites.md section 6.

third_party_invite_token_in_query: invite_token arrived in the URL query string or path segment (third-party-invites.md section 3.2); unsupported_join_rule: the intended Realm is knock_restricted, outside v1 base third-party claim (section 4.3). Token, invite and Realm existence failures stay non-enumerable (section 6).

No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. An unimplemented oob_code_kind or delivery scheme is unsupported_feature, a reused request_id with different canonical intent is duplicate_conflict, and anti-abuse refusals are rate_limited or quota_exceeded; none of them may reveal whether another inviter, Realm or 3PID exists.

No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. An unknown provisioning_id, a record belonging to another inviter and a deleted record MUST be indistinguishable (all not_found).

Exact Account Authority issuer-record replication. signature_invalid and unauthorized remain universal authentication failures. Ledger rejections use failed_precondition plus a closed reason_code: account_status_record_stale for lower sequence, account_status_record_fork for same-sequence different-record or next-sequence predecessor mismatch, account_status_binding_rollback for a lower binding_version, account_status_transition_invalid for an illegal lifecycle transition, and erasure_pending_is_terminal for a successor after the terminal state. Same Idempotency-Key with another canonical body alone is duplicate_conflict.
Unknown account, unrelated service and unauthorized caller share not_found before ledger disclosure;

Receipt package admission validates service/issuer authority, proofs, digest and retained-stub binding before acknowledgement or local deletion. Same idempotency key with another canonical body is duplicate_conflict.
Unknown, unauthorized and hidden receipt identifiers are deliberately indistinguishable as not_found.

Closed peer authority-forward, committed-replication and registered-atomic-unit ingress. Forward admission is evaluated by the current governance Station. Replication rejects unverifiable source Event/Commit coordinates, authority generation, chain, witness or visibility without re-signing or fanout. Direct Conversation founding and membership compensation are all-or-nothing; dependency_missing carries the registered closed details shape and no per-item partial is returned. A cross-Station human device producer is resolved only from authority_forward producer_device_evidence: a missing, surplus or malformed member is schema_violation, signature/key/Service-history or source-Station mismatch is signature_invalid, unauthorized device, out-of-window authorization or expired evidence is device_unauthorized, and revoked, revocation-pending and fenced devices use device_revoked, device_revocation_pending and device_generation_fenced. A forwarded ak.mls.genesis whose mls_genesis_material bytes do not hash to the Genesis group_info_ref or ratchet_tree_ref is digest_mismatch with zero writes; a missing or surplus mls_genesis_material is schema_violation. A carried Welcome that fails the destination's claim-ledger re-verification is not queued and does not reject the replicated Commit.

The destination KeyPackage authority exposes all target-, device-, inventory-, consent-, capability-, policy-, freshness-, and abuse-related business failures as claim_failed. duplicate_conflict covers claim_request_id reuse with another digest; failed_precondition is limited to a non-secret protocol-state violation that cannot reveal target inventory.

Read-only uncertain-outcome recovery. claim_failed is the opaque stored terminal failure; duplicate_conflict covers a known claim_request_id queried with a different request digest without returning target details.

Read-only single-hop directory fetch with no durable effect. Absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets are indistinguishable inside the typed 200 outcome, so no target-specific error code is exposed; transport authentication failures are decided before any target read and are identical for every selector.

Exact duplicate attestation replays its stored outcome; conflicting provenance, claim evidence or signer is rejected with zero historical-proof writes. A missing accepted dependency is revision_unavailable.

Replication-only reads retain dependency_missing, digest_mismatch, state_mismatch and limit_exceeded. With caller_actor_id, unauthorized and unknown selectors are uniformly not_found, while authorized missing or inconsistent historical material is uniformly revision_unavailable; the operation never returns partial material.

Unknown and unauthorized selectors share the universal not_found; incomplete or inconsistent history is uniformly revision_unavailable after authorization. A cursor from another caller, head or cut is invalid.
Authority-commit operation. Current authorization and stream-head checks are evaluated atomically by the current governance Station.

Unauthorized, nonexistent, expired/revoked/cross-account invite or currently disallowed policy share non-enumerating not_found and timing bucket, rechecked each page. Expired/lost context is cursor_expired; mismatched binding is cursor_integrity_invalid. Request identity conflict is duplicate_conflict. Missing accepted basis is revision_unavailable, missing graph record is dependency_missing. Each page is at most 8 MiB; record/context/work budget exhaustion is limit_exceeded with prior progress retained, never truncated success. Required but undisclosable private-scope material is revision_unavailable; an invite cannot override scope disclosure authorization.

Unknown Realm, unknown invite, an invite that does not bind the requested invitee, a source Station that is not the invitee's Station, a revoked or expired credential and a Realm without an effective preview policy all share one non-enumerating 404 not_found under the same fixed timing bucket. Request canonical bytes above 64 KiB are 413 payload_too_large.

Optional encrypted-only single-hop Signal peer relay. Only outer peer authentication, trust-domain/destination-endpoint checks, cross-Realm batches and malformed/oversized requests use the universal minimally disclosing failure surface. Per-item unknown Realm/scope/sender, producer-proof, current joined-member ActorId routing authority, TTL, action-gate, visibility, duplication and recipient failures are silently dropped behind the opaque accepted=true request outcome.

Establishes the local binding after verifying a method-native control or governance-quorum proof against a consumed challenge and a pinned resolved version. Every failure mode is a distinct registered code so a caller can tell a stale challenge from a bad proof from an insufficient quorum without parsing prose.
Issues a single-use control challenge for a resolvable external Organization DID. An unresolvable DID fails closed rather than yielding a challenge no proof could ever satisfy.
Re-proves control at a newer resolved version. A revoked binding is terminal and MUST NOT be revived by refresh; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure.
Withdraws the local binding only. Revoking an already-revoked binding is idempotent and returns the existing terminal receipt rather than an error.

Callers without authority over a binding receive the same did_not_found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the read surface cannot be used to enumerate a deployment's organization relationships.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Publishing or rotating a recovery policy requires authenticated principal isolation, valid Event/lease and the closed policy signature transcript/authority, a known proof-kind enum, and strictly monotonic version/supersedes linkage. revision_unavailable is the retry-safe response while the submitted Event is valid but its covering control RealmCommit/AuthorityRevision has not materialized.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. A missing accepted policy is a successful response with active_policy=null.
A session outside pending is rejected with recovery_session_not_pending; this is the machine carrier for the superseded terminal-session subreason.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
The Provider verifies a client-signed WebVH inception and returns the stable mapping for the canonical registration key. Conflicting control roots or hosted-document declarations fail closed.

Profile self-service accepts exactly one holder-signed ak.profile.create or ak.profile.update EventAdmissionSubmission. failed_precondition covers create against an existing Profile, update without an accepted Profile, target/PCR/session authority mismatch, expected_state_digest mismatch, and deterministic profile reducer guards. revision_unavailable is retry-safe while the valid Event lacks accepted RealmCommit coverage. Replaying the same Event identity with different bytes returns duplicate_conflict; exact replay after coverage returns the stored outcome without another aggregate delta. Update patch paths remain limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; avatar_url is rejected.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Holder-bound account self-read. If signed handle-claim evidence or profile/device source refs cannot be verified, the service MUST fail or omit the unverifiable evidence according to disclosure policy; it MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

cas_conflict when expected_server_revision does not equal the accepted per-key revision; the tombstone is not stored and error.details use account_data_cas_conflict_details. duplicate_conflict when the same Event identity arrives with different canonical Event bytes; zero writes.
not_found carries account_data_cas_conflict_details so a caller reading an unset or tombstoned key still learns current_revision for its next compare-and-set write.

cas_conflict when expected_server_revision does not equal the accepted per-key revision; error.details use account_data_cas_conflict_details so the client can merge and re-issue exactly one write. duplicate_conflict when the same Event identity arrives with different canonical Event bytes; zero writes.

duplicate_conflict when the same Event identity or occupied create-once key arrives with different canonical Event bytes; cas_conflict when an ak.device.push_route expected_server_revision does not equal the accepted revision; failed_precondition when an ak.agent.action_reject target is missing, terminal or not rejectable, or an agent proposal or request is expired. All with zero writes. Wrong owner Station is param_invalid and binding, capability or policy refusal is capability_denied (universal).

No operation-specific error codes. Per-actor outcomes are carried in the response failures array with the single value profile_unavailable; unknown actor, missing profile, non-member actor and unauthorized caller are indistinguishable. A caller that is not an effective joined member of realm_id receives not_found for the whole request.

agent_deactivated is returned for idempotent re-deactivation of an already-terminal Agent. Missing or invalid proof on the sole controller-authored lifecycle Event returns controller_signed_event_required. Once that Event is accepted, the terminal parent lifecycle gate immediately makes every child authorization ineffective; client-supplied key/grant revoke bundles are schema-invalid and asynchronous cleanup failure cannot roll back deactivation.
agent_paused is returned for idempotent re-pause; agent_deactivated is terminal. A lifecycle Event without its required controller proof returns controller_signed_event_required.

Provision an Agent principal. The controller first publishes a PCR-independent Agent DID inception. prepare verifies its caller-supplied did and returns the exact accepted initial_resolution plus an allocation without generating a DID/private key or choosing a PCR id. commit accepts exactly one controller-signed ak.agent.provision Event that forward-declares the realm id derived from the locally frozen genesis create, atomically projects provision/accountability/selector/realm-id-claim and returns awaiting_pcr_genesis. Separate PCR acceptance advances to awaiting_did_binding; only the controller-signed continuous DID entry 1 with the exact create-locked binding advances to complete and exposes pairing/list/get. requested_scope is a ceiling, not a grant; the service never generates Agent DID/PCR/MLS private state.

Re-open bootstrap pairing or replace an Agent runtime. A renewed pairing MUST issue a fresh single-use `pairing_request_id` + `pairing_code` and MUST leave every previously issued handle permanently unresolvable. An Agent without an active accepted runtime-key authorization uses bootstrap; an Agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle `active` or `paused`) uses replacement, whose single controller-signed authorize Event atomically supersedes prior authorization dots while preserving lifecycle intent. Generic views expose open-handle fields and readiness blockers, never runtime_state. `deactivated` returns `agent_deactivated`. Neither branch creates, revokes, or re-issues Realm grants; handle expiry has no side effects beyond clearing open-handle fields and recomputing readiness.

Resume revalidates controller, agent key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability grant freshness; any stale precondition fails closed. Sidecar desired membership is re-derived after admission and is not a request precondition. A lifecycle Event without its required controller proof returns controller_signed_event_required.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
expected_version must equal the Account Authority's current version for the exact agent/scope slot. First write uses zero; a mismatch returns cas_conflict and performs no write.
not_found is returned both for nonexistent agent principals and for agents not visible to the caller (uniform failure surface, matches ak.self.committed_event.resource.get.v1 pattern).

Idempotent ensure: the protocol identity key is `(realm_id, controller_account_id)` for the Agent Sidecar; `(sidecar_id, normalized_source_context_ref)` deduplicates context mappings without creating another protocol object. `agent_id` is not part of either key. Clients MUST NOT supply Idempotency-Key. sidecar_create_denied is a deliberately generic existence-privacy precondition.
Returns only authenticated-controller-owned Sidecars; another controller's objects do not appear as locked stubs or distinguishable omissions.
Nonexistent, foreign-controller, and unauthorized Sidecar identifiers return the same not_found envelope and timing bucket.

Applet install commit recomputes the InstallPlan, binds approval to plan_digest, persists fan-out idempotency state, and emits registration/grant/profile/membership facts. Recomputing the plan re-runs the actor namespace pattern shape and exclusive conflict checks, so a package that previewed cleanly against a stale view still fails closed here with the same codes.
Applet revoke validates caller-signed revoke/member submissions against a fresh plan, then resumes a durable event/external/local saga; the first accepted revoke fences future writes.

The active Applet service supplies only the requested Realm, exact external tuple and optional display name. The Station derives all current installation coordinates and fails closed if the pinned registration epoch is deactivated or the Realm is outside current authorization.

Ghost Actor provisioning atomically accepts (or idempotently re-confirms) the caller-signed fixed four-Event unit: ak.applet.managed_actor.provision, the applet_managed_control PCR ak.realm.create genesis, ak.identity.accountability_grant, and ak.profile.create. The unit freezes the exact account ActorId, registration/grant authority, initial resolution, PCR lineage, accountability, and external principal tuple. The server never signs for the Applet service or Ghost. It fails closed on invalid proofs/checkpoints, a caller service DID that does not match the active applet registration, a realm outside effective scope (applet_registration_unauthorized), or a ghost_actor_id outside the registered actor namespace (applet_namespace_mismatch). See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §9.1.

Applet install preview validates controller proof, package schema, DID/key binding, actor namespace pattern shape, namespace conflicts, requested capability actions, and Realm/Circle policy before returning an InstallPlan. An actor namespace pattern that is not did:webvh, pins the registration's own service SCID, carries a non-literal host segment, or has no segment after the host is applet_namespace_pattern_invalid; a wildcard-versus-wildcard exclusive collision with another applet_id's active claim is applet_namespace_conflict.
Applet revoke preview recomputes the exact current active-grant, managed-membership, and widget-token plan without side effects.
Missing or malformed realm_id or subject_actor_id uses universal param_invalid; unknown or unauthorized exact actors remain non-enumerable.

Two-phase holder-local Contact request acceptance stores one signed fact and its source receipt. Target resolution and delivery occur later through the receipted peer carrier, so an unresolved target does not reject prepare. It writes no Private Consent and conflicts on byte drift, slot reuse or an already-consumed request ref; revision_unavailable is retry-safe while the holder PCR actor or accepted RealmCommit checkpoint is unavailable.
Only the request target may sign a normal acceptance. Glare, late reverse requests, slot conflicts and consumed refs fail closed; rejection uses the separate reject operation.
Issuer-local version/predecessor conflicts quarantine; stale current proof cannot authorize an update or subsequent Contact-based create/send.
A holder-signed tombstone ends one issuer-local Contact generation and cannot be replayed as a scope replacement or Private Consent revocation.
Holder Contact projection from the two holder-signed directional Contact lineages; Consent is never an authority source.

Idempotent resolver for a pair's one stable conversation. Existing conversations return found or suspended without a KeyPackage lookup. Endpoint-specific self authority-commit union. Ordinary and MLS branches keep single-submit semantics; Direct Conversation founding atomically commits exactly four ordered Events into four consecutive RealmCommits and returns no second receipt; membership compensation verifies transport-only evidence and claims its single-use CAS in the same Event transaction. A human device producer is resolved from the local PCR when this Station governs the target; otherwise the account Station refuses to forward an unusable device with device_unauthorized, device_revoked, device_revocation_pending or device_generation_fenced.

Closed message preparation. Encrypted content into a definitely inactive scope returns generic failed_precondition without writes; unreadable current MLS state returns universal temporarily_unavailable and allows exact retry only before a Commit. An MLS request whose frozen epoch, group_state_ref or key_access_revision differs from a ready current group returns top-level epoch_mismatch (HTTP 409); if the current key-access checkpoint awaits a winning Commit, failed_precondition with epoch_update_required takes precedence and the client pauses. Expired preparation requires a new identity and never changes accepted Event validity.

not_found is the single anti-oracle result for an absent target, a target not visible to the reporter, or any declared Realm/effective-scope mismatch. evidence_recipient_mismatch rejects a canonical evidence package whose recipient_public_key_ref and encrypted_to differ or whose key is not authorized for the exact target scope. Exact replay of one accepted report Event returns the stored submitted outcome; reuse of the same Event identity with different canonical bytes returns duplicate_conflict and appends neither a report log entry nor a queue item.

An account or Station that does not match the authenticated session, an unknown or hidden Realm, an invalid, expired or revoked invite credential and a join policy that does not admit the declared intent share one non-enumerating 404 not_found. A basis, digest suite or encryption profile that cannot currently be obtained and verified is 503 revision_unavailable and never a defaulted value. A pre-state that no longer holds under the current accepted basis is 409 failed_precondition and requires a fresh preparation, never a rewrite of already signed material. Request canonical bytes above 64 KiB are 413 payload_too_large. A required authority-stream head or admission basis that cannot be derived is 503 revision_unavailable and never a defaulted position=0. For an otherwise disclosable target, no verifiable current governance Station, unreachable candidates, or candidate evidence that cannot establish one consistent verified authority return revision_unavailable (503), with no draft or default basis.
